claim: In the generalized timing law \(nt=\chi-\tilde e\sin\chi\), the coefficient consistent with Lynden-Bell's derived central-orbit timing formula is \(\tilde e=(V_2/V_1)e^*\), not the reciprocal \((V_1/V_2)e^*\) printed in the 2014 inversion paper. With the paper's stated definitions, the exact harmonic-orbit case \(k=2\) has \(V_1=1-(e^*)^2\) and \(V_2=0\): the printed coefficient is undefined, whereas the corrected coefficient is zero and gives the exact linear timing \(nt=\chi\). The Kepler case \(k=1\), where \(V_1=V_2=1\), is unchanged.

integrity.evidence_basis: Direct comparison of two open full-text primary papers plus symbolic evaluation of their shared coefficient definitions at \(k=1\) and \(k=2\).
integrity.novelty_limit: Bounded semantic literature-record and public-literature searches found no matching correction; unindexed correspondence or errata may exist.

scientific_limitations: Corrects only the reciprocal coefficient in the displayed generalized timing law.
Does not certify the full approximate timing theory for arbitrary central potentials or give a global error bound for the cubic solver.
The 2015 source states that small terms are omitted in the general case; the Kepler and harmonic boundary cases \(k=1\) and \(k=2\) used here are exact.
title: The reciprocal coefficient in generalized Kepler timing
